name: Blink the LED
desc: Red LED blinks once a second using millis() instead of delay().

name: Two-LED Alternate Flasher
desc: Red and green flash alternately like a railway crossing.

name: Button-Controlled LED
desc: Hold the push button to light the LED (INPUT_PULLUP, pressed = LOW).

name: Toggle Latch Switch
desc: Each press toggles the green LED; edge detection with debounce.

name: Slide-Switch Mode Select
desc: The slide switch picks a slow or fast blink (click the lever while running).

name: Potentiometer Brightness Dimmer
desc: The pot sets the PWM brightness of the green LED.

name: RGB Colour Cycle
desc: Steps through red, green, blue and mixed colours.

name: Active Buzzer Beeper
desc: Short press = short beep, hold longer = long beep.

name: Piezo Tone Scale
desc: Plays C-D-E-F-G-A-B-C with tone() on the passive buzzer.

name: Serial Monitor Hello and Echo
desc: Prints a greeting, echoes what you type in the Serial tab and blinks the LED per byte.

name: Traffic Light Controller
desc: Green, yellow and red LEDs in a timed non-blocking state machine.

name: Pedestrian Crossing
desc: Press the button: cars stop, buzzer ticks, then traffic resumes.

name: Pot-Controlled RGB Mixer
desc: The button picks R, G or B; the pot sets that channel.

name: LED Fade Breathing Effect
desc: A sine-shaped fade mimics breathing.

name: Knight Rider Scanner
desc: Light sweeps between red and green by cross-fading; the pot sets the speed.

name: LDR Night Lamp
desc: The green lamp turns on automatically when the LDR reading says it is dark.

name: Adjustable Dark Threshold
desc: Pot sets the darkness level that switches the lamp; hysteresis avoids flicker.

name: Light-Controlled Dimmer
desc: The darker the room, the brighter the red LED.

name: Light Theremin
desc: The light level on the LDR changes the pitch on the piezo.

name: Pot Theremin
desc: The pot sets a continuous pitch; the button silences it.

name: Simple Melody Player
desc: Press the button to play 'Happy Birthday' from note and duration tables.

name: Morse Code Sender
desc: Type text in the Serial tab and it is blinked and beeped as Morse.

name: Button Counter with LED Binary Display
desc: Count presses 0-3 and show the count in binary on red (bit 0) and green (bit 1).

name: Reaction Timer
desc: Wait for the green LED and beep, press as fast as you can; time shown in ms.

name: Door-Open Reminder
desc: The slide switch is a door contact: left open for 5 s and the buzzer reminds you.

name: Colour Mood Lamp
desc: RGB lamp drifts through the colour wheel; the button freezes the colour.

name: Rotary Volume Bar Simulator
desc: Pot value shown as percent, a text bar and a 2-LED level indicator.

name: Strobe with Adjustable Rate
desc: Pot sets 1-20 Hz; the slide switch picks the red or green LED.

name: Auto Alarm Siren
desc: Hold the button: a two-tone siren sweeps up and down on the piezo.

name: Serial LED Command Console
desc: Type commands in the Serial tab: r1, g0, c 255 0 40 (RGB colour).

name: Four-Way Intersection Simulator
desc: Two-road signal with pedestrian request, ticking buzzer and automatic night flashing from the LDR (or the slide switch).

name: Reaction Game with High Score
desc: Best time is saved in EEPROM; the RGB colour shows your rank; buzzer feedback.

name: Simon Says Memory Game
desc: Repeat the growing red/green pattern with the two buttons; RGB shows your level.

name: Digital Lock with Button Code
desc: Unlock with a short-long-short-short press code; wrong code sounds the alarm.

name: Automatic Day/Night Controller with Hysteresis
desc: A warm RGB lamp fades in at night with pot-set sensitivity; the button overrides.

name: Musical Instrument: Pot Keyboard
desc: The pot picks a note over two octaves, the button plays it, and the RGB colour shows the note.

name: Light-Following Tone Alarm (Security Beam)
desc: Arm with the slide switch; breaking the light beam latches the alarm until reset.

name: Software PWM Chaser
desc: Gamma-corrected brightness profiles are computed in software and chased across four LEDs; pot = speed.

name: Finite-State-Machine Vending Demo
desc: Button = coin, pot picks the item price; the machine dispenses and returns change.

name: Metronome with Tempo Memory
desc: Pot sets 40-208 BPM; accent every 4th beat; the button stores the tempo in EEPROM.

name: Binary and Gray-Code Counter Trainer
desc: Count 0-15 on 4 LEDs; the slide switch toggles binary / Gray code.

name: Debounce and Long-Press Library
desc: One button, three gestures: click = next colour, double-click = off, long press = brightness.

name: Dark Room Intruder Logger
desc: Watches for sudden light flashes in a dark room, logs severity and time over Serial, and beeps accordingly.

name: Pot-to-Tone Encoder
desc: Encodes the pot reading as 4 tone pulses (high = 1, low = 0); Serial Plotter shows pot, code and ambient light.

name: Interactive Story Lamp
desc: Four colour scenes (dawn, forest, sunset, storm). Button = next, slide = auto-advance, pot = brightness.

name: Two-Player Quick-Draw Game
desc: First to hit their button after the BEEP wins (red = player 1, green = player 2); jumping the gun loses.

name: Sunrise Alarm Clock Simulator
desc: The RGB lamp slowly brightens over a pot-set time, then the buzzer wakes you; button = snooze / stop.

name: Self-Calibrating Light Meter
desc: First 5 s record the min / max light; then the meter shows relative brightness. Button re-calibrates.

name: Three-Mode Menu System
desc: Button = next LED program (alternate / colour fade / chaser); slide switch = slow / fast; mode shown by blink count.

name: Security Panel Simulator
desc: Long-press to arm / disarm, slide switch = door contact, entry delay, then siren. RGB shows the status.

name: Room Temperature Reader (LM35)
desc: Converts the LM35 voltage to degrees Celsius. Change the temperature in the inspector.

name: DHT11 Temperature and Humidity Display
desc: Reads temperature and humidity with the DHT library every 2 s.

name: Thermistor Raw Reading
desc: Reads the NTC in a voltage divider and prints the ADC value and resistance.

name: Light Level Reader
desc: Prints the LDR reading and a Bright / Dim / Dark label.

name: Soil Moisture Reader
desc: Classifies the soil as dry, moist or wet.

name: Rain Detector
desc: Lights the red LED and prints RAIN when the sensor board gets wet.

name: Clap Switch
desc: A loud clap toggles the green LED (raise the sound level in the inspector).

name: Pot Threshold Setter
desc: Prints the pot as a 0-100 % setting whenever it changes.

name: Over-Temperature Buzzer
desc: The buzzer sounds when the LM35 reads more than 35 C.

name: Button-Triggered Sensor Reading
desc: Press the button to take a one-shot DHT11 reading.

name: Thermistor Temperature (Steinhart-Hart)
desc: Real temperature from the NTC using the beta / Steinhart-Hart equation.

name: LM35 vs Thermistor Comparison
desc: Both sensors side by side with their difference.

name: Heat Index Calculator
desc: Combines temperature and humidity into a "feels like" heat index.

name: Comfort Indicator
desc: Green = comfortable, yellow = borderline, red = uncomfortable (temperature and humidity).

name: Plant Watering Alert
desc: Red LED and beeps when moisture falls below the pot-set threshold.

name: Rain Warning with Intensity
desc: Light / moderate / heavy rain give 1, 2 or 3 beeps.

name: Auto Street Light
desc: The street lamp (red LED) switches on in the dark; the pot sets the level, hysteresis stops flicker.

name: Clap Counter
desc: One clap = green, two = red, three = both, within a 1.5 s window.

name: Sound Level Meter
desc: Peak level over a 50 ms window as 0-100, with a text bar and LEDs.

name: Fever Alarm
desc: Average of 10 LM35 samples against a pot-set limit (35-42 C).

name: Dew Point Estimator
desc: Dew point with the Magnus formula; red LED when condensation is likely.

name: Soil + Light Plant Monitor
desc: Green = happy plant, red = needs water, yellow = needs light.

name: Moving-Average Filter Demo
desc: Raw vs 10-sample moving average, ready for the Serial Plotter.

name: Min/Max Recorder
desc: Tracks the lowest and highest temperature since power-up; the button resets them.

name: Humidity Alarm
desc: Alarm when the humidity goes above the pot-set limit (30-90 %).

name: Dark and Quiet Detector
desc: Green when the room is both dark and quiet (bedtime detector).

name: Rain-Triggered Cover Indicator
desc: Cover closes (green) after 3 s of rain and reopens (red) after 10 s dry.

name: Sensor Calibration Helper
desc: Button records the dry then the wet reading, stores both in EEPROM and shows a calibrated percentage.

name: Thermistor Fan-Trigger Indicator
desc: Pot sets the target (20-40 C); green = fan on, red = fan off, with 1 C hysteresis.

name: Multi-Sensor Serial Dashboard
desc: One tidy line with temperature, humidity, light and sound for logging.

name: Smart Plant Care Station
desc: Scores water, light and temperature; green / yellow / red status, buzzer when critical. Pot sets the moisture target.

name: Mini Weather Station
desc: Temperature, humidity, rain and light summarised into a forecast string.

name: Environmental Data Logger
desc: Time-stamped CSV lines for all sensors; the button marks an event in the log.

name: Frost and Overheat Guard
desc: Two independent sensors, dual thresholds, a latched fault and an acknowledge button.

name: Auto Greenhouse Logic
desc: Rule engine: yellow = watering, red = vent / cooling, green = grow light. Pot sets the temperature limit.

name: Clap-Pattern Door Knock Code
desc: Secret knock: clap, short pause, clap, long pause, clap. Right pattern lights green, wrong sounds the buzzer.

name: Rain and Humidity Storm Predictor
desc: Rising humidity plus rain onset triggers a storm warning with trend analysis.

name: Thermistor Linearisation and Self-Test
desc: Button stores the LM35 as a reference; the NTC is corrected with the offset and an error table is printed.

name: Night Garden Watering Scheduler
desc: Green = watering. It waters only when it is dark, the soil is dry and it is not raining; red shows it is blocked.

name: Sound-Reactive Light Show
desc: Four LEDs climb with the sound level; pot = sensitivity; the buzzer beats on very loud peaks.

name: Comfort Index Display with Trend Arrows
desc: Shows temperature and humidity trends as ^ v = arrows; the button switches which metric the LEDs follow.

name: Sensor Health Monitor
desc: Detects missing or stuck sensors; the red LED blinks a fault code (1 = DHT, 2 = LM35, 3 = soil), green when all is well.

name: Statistical Sensor Analyzer
desc: Collects 100 LM35 samples and reports mean, variance, standard deviation and drift; the button re-runs it.

name: Wet-Dry Calibration Wizard
desc: Guided wizard calibrates soil and rain sensors (dry then wet), saves them in EEPROM and prints a summary.

name: Occupancy Estimator (Sound + Light)
desc: Scores noise events and light changes over time; green = room occupied, red = vacant.

name: Dual-Sensor Fusion Thermometer
desc: Weighted fusion of DHT11 and LM35 with outlier rejection.

name: Alert Escalation System
desc: Warning (yellow) -> alarm (red) -> critical (red + fast buzzer) from temperature, noise and light.

name: Daily Climate Report Generator
desc: Accelerated day: 1 "hour" = 1 s. After 24 samples prints a formatted table with min / max / average.

name: Smart Humidity-Rain Dehumidifier Logic
desc: State machine with minimum on/off times; green = dehumidifier on. Pot sets the target humidity; rain raises the demand.

name: Dry-Spell Early Warning
desc: Measures how fast the soil is drying and predicts the time until the critical level; warns early.

name: Hello World on LCD
desc: Shows 'Hello, JR Learners' on the 16x2 I2C LCD.

name: LCD Counter
desc: Counts up once a second on the LCD.

name: OLED Text Display
desc: Prints text lines in two sizes on the SSD1306 OLED.

name: TM1637 Number Display
desc: Counts 0000-9999 on the 4-digit display.

name: LED Matrix Smiley
desc: Draws a smiley face on the 8x8 MAX7219 matrix.

name: 74HC595 LED Counter
desc: Counts 0-255 in binary on 8 LEDs through the shift register.

name: Rotary Encoder Counter
desc: Counts clockwise / counter-clockwise detents and prints them. Use the inspector buttons to turn the knob.

name: Joystick Axis Reader
desc: Prints the X, Y and button state of the joystick.

name: Button Count on TM1637
desc: Every button press adds one to the 7-segment counter.

name: LCD Backlight Control
desc: The push button toggles the LCD backlight.

name: Scrolling Text on LCD
desc: A long message scrolls across the second row of the 16x2 display like a marquee.

name: Digital Stopwatch (TM1637)
desc: Short press = start / stop. Hold the button for 1 s while stopped = reset. Shows SS:hh (seconds and hundredths).

name: Countdown Timer
desc: Turn the encoder to set MM:SS (5 s per click), push the shaft to start. At zero the display and red LED flash.

name: Joystick-Controlled Dot on Matrix
desc: Move one LED around the 8x8 matrix with the joystick. Hold the joystick button to leave a trail.

name: Scrolling Marquee on Matrix
desc: Scrolls a message across the 8x8 matrix using a 5x7 font table.

name: 74HC595 Knight Rider
desc: A two-LED scanner bounces back and forth across the 8 LEDs.

name: Binary Clock Display
desc: Seconds counter in binary on the 8 LEDs and in decimal on the LCD.

name: Encoder Menu on LCD
desc: Scroll a 4-item menu with the encoder and select with its push switch.

name: OLED Bar Graph
desc: Live bar and scrolling history of the joystick X axis on the OLED.

name: OLED Analog Clock Face (software clock)
desc: Analog clock with hour, minute and second hands driven by millis(), plus a digital readout.

name: Digital Dice
desc: Press the button to roll: a short shuffle, then the die face on the matrix and the running total on the TM1637.

name: Scoreboard
desc: One button, two teams: a short press scores for team A, a long press (over 0.6 s) for team B. Shows AA:BB.

name: Etch-A-Sketch on OLED
desc: Draw with the joystick (push it past centre to move the pen); the push button clears the screen.

name: LCD Custom Characters
desc: Defines your own 5x8 characters: a beating heart, a charging battery and a moving arrow.

name: LED Bar Level Indicator
desc: The joystick Y position lights 0-8 LEDs as a bar through the 74HC595.

name: Number Guessing Game
desc: Dial a guess (1-100) with the encoder, press the button to try. The LCD says TOO LOW / TOO HIGH until you win.

name: Matrix Animation Player
desc: Plays animations stored in a table: a heartbeat, then falling rain.

name: TM1637 Brightness and Colon Demo
desc: Uptime MM:SS with a blinking colon; the encoder sets the display brightness (0-7).

name: Serial-to-OLED Text Terminal
desc: Type in the Serial Monitor and the text appears on the OLED; it scrolls when the screen is full.

name: Reaction Time Game on LCD
desc: Press to start, wait for the green LED, then press as fast as you can. The LCD shows your time and best time.

name: Pixel Pong Game
desc: Pong on the 8x8 matrix: the encoder moves the 3-LED paddle, the TM1637 shows your score. Press the button to serve.

name: Snake Game
desc: Snake on the 8x8 matrix steered by the joystick; the TM1637 counts apples. Walls and your own tail are deadly.

name: OLED Video Game: Breakout
desc: Breakout on the OLED: the encoder moves the paddle, the button launches the ball, the LCD shows lives and score.

name: Multi-Page Info Dashboard
desc: Turn the encoder to flip between Uptime, Joystick and Counters pages on the OLED while the LCD names the page.

name: Digital Clock with Alarm Set
desc: Software clock on the TM1637. Button cycles RUN / set hour / set minute / alarm hour / alarm minute; the encoder changes the value. The alarm flashes the red and green LEDs.

name: Matrix Equaliser Visualizer
desc: Eight animated spectrum bars on the matrix. Joystick up/down = level (gain), left/right = animation speed.

name: Shift-Register Cascade Engine
desc: Six LED animation patterns on the 74HC595. Joystick left/right picks the pattern, the encoder sets the speed.

name: Tic-Tac-Toe on OLED
desc: Two players share the board: the joystick moves the cursor, the button places X or O. The LCD keeps the score.

name: Menu-Driven Settings System
desc: Two-level menu on the LCD (encoder = move / click, button = back). Settings are stored in EEPROM and previewed live on the OLED.

name: Game of Life on 8x8 Matrix
desc: Conway's Life with wrap-around edges. Edit mode: joystick moves the blinking cursor, its button flips a cell. The push button starts / pauses; the TM1637 shows the generation.

name: Calculator with Joystick Keypad
desc: Joystick left/right picks a key (0-9 + - * / = C), the joystick button types it, the push button is backspace. Evaluated left to right, whole numbers.

name: Binary-Hex-Decimal Converter Trainer
desc: Dial a number 0-255 with the encoder (push = step 1 / step 16). The 8 LEDs show binary, the TM1637 hex, the LCD decimal and binary.

name: Scrolling News Ticker with Speed Control
desc: The headline scrolls across the matrix (5x7 font) and the OLED together. Turn the encoder to change the speed.

name: OLED Oscilloscope Simulator
desc: Scrolling sine / sawtooth / square waves. The encoder sets the frequency, the button changes the waveform.

name: Memory Card Game
desc: Sixteen hidden cards (each a 2x2 block of the matrix, 8 pairs of patterns). Joystick picks a card, the button flips it; the LCD counts moves and pairs.

name: Lap Timer with Best-Lap Record
desc: First press starts the timer, each later press records a lap. The TM1637 shows the running lap time, the LCD the last and best lap. Hold the button for 1 s to reset.

name: Pixel Art Editor
desc: Joystick moves the cursor, its button flips a pixel, the push button saves the picture as the next frame (up to 8). Encoder turn = browse frames, encoder push = play / stop the animation (turn = speed).

name: Bargraph VU on 74HC595 + OLED Trace
desc: A simulated audio level drives the 8-LED VU bar with a peak-hold LED, while the OLED plots the level history. Joystick up/down = gain.

name: Mini Operating Console
desc: Boot animation across all four displays, then three apps - Clock, Dice, Counter. Turn the encoder to switch apps, press the button to use them.

name: Joystick Typing Trainer
desc: Spell the target word letter by letter: joystick left/right = previous / next letter, up/down = jump 5, push button = type it. The LCD shows accuracy and speed.

name: Ultrasonic Distance Meter
desc: Measures distance in cm with the HC-SR04 and prints it. Move the obstacle slider in the inspector.

name: PIR Motion LED
desc: The red LED lights whenever the PIR sees motion (tick "Motion detected" in the inspector).

name: Obstacle Detector
desc: The IR obstacle sensor lights the red LED when an object is in front of it.

name: Touch Switch
desc: Each touch of the TTP223 pad toggles the green LED.

name: Magnet Door Sensor
desc: The Hall sensor lights the red LED while a magnet is near (a magnet on the door, the sensor on the frame).

name: Servo Sweep
desc: Sweeps the SG90 servo from 0 to 180 degrees and back.

name: Line Detector
desc: The TCRT5000 reports a black line vs a white surface; the green LED lights over the line. Change "Surface reflectivity" in the inspector.

name: ToF Distance Reader
desc: Prints the distance in millimetres from the VL53L0X laser sensor.

name: Distance Beeper
desc: The piezo beeps faster the closer the object is.

name: Button-Controlled Servo
desc: Each button press steps the servo by 30 degrees; after 180 it returns to 0.

name: Parking Sensor
desc: Like a car parking aid: green = plenty of room, green + red = getting close, red + faster beeps = very close, steady tone under 10 cm.

name: Motion Alarm
desc: Button arms the alarm after a 5 s exit delay (red blinks fast). Armed = red steady. Motion starts the siren; the button disarms.

name: Servo Radar Scanner
desc: The servo turns the ultrasonic sensor in 10 degree steps and prints angle,distance pairs for each sweep.

name: Automatic Door Opener
desc: A person seen by the PIR or closer than 30 cm to the ultrasonic sensor opens the 'door' (servo to 90 degrees); it closes 3 s after the last sighting.

name: Touch-Activated Servo Lock
desc: Touch toggles the servo bolt between LOCKED (0 degrees, red) and UNLOCKED (90 degrees, green).

name: Line-Follower Sensor Test Bench
desc: Shows line / no-line live. Calibrate with the button: press over white, press over black, and the threshold is set halfway. A third press resets.

name: Obstacle-Avoid Servo Steering Demo
desc: The servo is the car's steering: straight (90) when clear, left (45) when the ultrasonic sees something within 40 cm, hard right (135) when the IR sensor sees something very close.

name: People Counter
desc: Counts objects passing the IR sensor; the button resets the count.

name: Door Open/Close Logger
desc: The Hall sensor + magnet log door events with timestamps. Green = closed, red = open, and the buzzer beeps if the door stays open for over 5 s.

name: Ultrasonic Level Meter
desc: The sensor sits 5 cm above a 30 cm tank and measures the distance to the surface. Prints the level as a percentage bar; red when the tank is nearly empty (<10 %) or nearly full (>90 %).

name: Gesture Switch
desc: Wave your hand in to within 20 cm to toggle the green LED. Take the hand away (beyond 35 cm) to re-arm.

name: Millimetre Ruler
desc: VL53L0X distance averaged over 8 readings. Press the button to zero the ruler at the current distance.

name: Speed Estimator
desc: Two sensors 10 cm apart form two gates. Time between the IR sensor and the line sensor triggering gives the speed. Trigger the IR obstacle first, then lower the line sensor reflectivity.

name: Motion-Triggered Servo Camera Pan
desc: While the PIR sees motion the servo pans slowly left and right; when motion stops it holds its position.

name: Touch Piano
desc: Each tap on the TTP223 plays the next note of the C major scale; your hand height above the ToF sensor picks the octave (close = high, far = low).

name: Proximity Light Switch
desc: The IR obstacle sensor switches the green LED on; the ToF distance dims it - the closer the hand, the brighter.

name: Edge/Cliff Detector
desc: The TCRT5000 looks down at the table. When the table disappears (reflectivity drops) the red LED and a two-tone alarm start.

name: Bike Wheel Revolution Counter
desc: The Hall sensor counts magnet passes. Every 2 s it prints rpm and speed for a 2.1 m wheel; the button resets the total.

name: Servo Position Memory
desc: Hold the button to jog the servo (it reverses direction each time), tap it to save the pose (up to 5). After the 5th pose the servo replays them in a loop (green LED); press once to clear and start over.

name: PIR Occupancy Timer
desc: The light stays on for a hold time after the last motion and the timer restarts on every new motion. (10 s here; set HOLD_MS to 300000 for 5 minutes.)

name: Servo Radar with Object Map
desc: The servo sweeps both rangers through 180 degrees in 5 degree steps and streams angle, ultrasonic cm, ToF cm as CSV for the Serial Plotter, then reports the nearest object of each sweep.

name: Smart Parking Assistant
desc: Fuses the ultrasonic and ToF readings, smooths them with integer (fixed-point) filtering, then drives LEDs and beeps. Under 15 cm = STOP (steady tone). The button mutes the buzzer.

name: Intruder Detection System
desc: Three zones: door (Hall + magnet, with 8 s entry delay), room motion (PIR) and a 80 cm ultrasonic tripwire (instant alarm). Arm / disarm by tapping the touch pad short-long-short. 8 s exit delay.

name: Automatic Gate Controller
desc: State machine CLOSED - OPENING - OPEN - CLOSING. A vehicle within 40 cm opens the gate; it closes 4 s after the road is clear. The Hall sensor (magnet on the gate) confirms CLOSED; the IR sensor in the gateway re-opens a closing gate.

name: Line Follower Decision Logic
desc: The analog line sensor follows the edge of a line: a PID controller turns the error into a steering angle on the servo. The button calibrates white then black. Green = on the edge, red = line lost.

name: Sonar Mapping Robot Brain (Bench)
desc: The servo points the ultrasonic sensor in 5 directions and the robot "decides" to go where it is clearest: green = forward, red = turn (steady = left, blinking = right), red + beeps = blocked, STOP.

name: Touch + Distance Gesture Panel
desc: Touch selects the mode (1 = green brightness, 2 = red brightness, 3 = pitch) and the piezo beeps the mode number; your hand distance over the ToF sensor sets the value (close = high).

name: Hand-Proximity Theremin
desc: One hand over the ToF sensor sets the pitch (close = high); the ultrasonic distance sets a "volume": the piezo is driven with longer bursts when the second hand is closer.

name: RPM Meter with Hall Sensor
desc: Measures the time between magnet passes, averages the last 5 and shows rpm. Over the limit = red + beeps, otherwise green. The button cycles the limit (60 / 120 / 180 rpm).

name: Elevator Floor Simulator
desc: The servo is the elevator car (floor 1 = 0, floor 2 = 90, floor 3 = 180 degrees). Tap the button 1-3 times to call that floor; calls are queued. Red = moving, green = doors open (held open while the IR door sensor is blocked), chime on arrival.

name: Vehicle Speed Trap
desc: Two gates 20 cm apart (IR sensor, then line sensor). The time between them gives the speed of a toy car; over 40 cm/s the buzzer sounds and the red LED lights, otherwise green. Trigger the IR first, then lower the line-sensor reflectivity.

name: Water-Tank Level Controller Model
desc: Level from the ultrasonic distance (30 cm tank). Pump (green LED) switches ON below 25 % and OFF above 85 % (hysteresis). If the level does not rise 3 % within 8 s of pumping, a dry-run alarm latches (red + siren) until the button resets it.

name: Smart Dustbin
desc: A hand seen by the IR sensor or the PIR opens the lid (servo 90 degrees, green LED) for 3 s. With the lid closed the ultrasonic sensor looks into the bin: closer than 8 cm = FULL (red LED).

name: Distance-Based Security Zones
desc: Three nested zones: 1 notice (green blinks), 2 warning (red blinks + slow beeps), 3 alarm (red steady + siren). The button cycles zone presets (150/100/50, 100/60/30, 60/40/20 cm). Every change is logged with a timestamp.

name: Servo Plotter Calibration Tool
desc: Press the button: the servo steps through 0-180 degrees in 15 degree steps, the ToF sensor averages 5 readings at each angle, and the table plus a least-squares fit (mm per degree) is printed. Change the target distance while it runs to see the curve.

name: Motion-Aware Night Lamp
desc: The PIR fades the green lamp up quickly and, 8 s after the last motion, fades it out slowly (PWM). A touch toggles an "always on" override, shown by a dim red LED.

name: Gesture Counter Game
desc: Press the button for a 15 s challenge. Every swipe past the IR sensor and every hand-in/hand-out within 25 cm of the ultrasonic sensor scores a point with a tick. At the end the buzzer plays one beep per point (up to 10).

name: Door Ajar and Tamper Detector
desc: Press the button to authorise opening (10 s). Opening the door WITHOUT it, 4+ door changes within 2 s (tampering), or motion beside an unauthorised open door latches the alarm (red + siren) until the button resets it with the door closed. An authorised door left open > 10 s beeps "ajar".

name: Multi-Sensor Fusion Distance Estimator
desc: Combines ultrasonic, ToF and the IR proximity sensor. Agreeing ultrasonic + ToF = HIGH confidence (green), one sensor only or disagreement = MEDIUM (both LEDs), the IR sensor contradicting the range = LOW (red).

name: Assistive Cane Prototype
desc: Beeps faster as an obstacle gets closer (within 150 cm). The TCRT5000 pointing at the floor detects a drop-off and sounds a different continuous alarm with the red LED. The button mutes obstacle beeps (never the drop alarm); green blinks as a heartbeat.

name: Servo Sweep
desc: Sweeps the SG90 servo through its full range, 0 to 180 degrees and back.

name: DC Motor On/Off with Transistor
desc: The button toggles the 6 V motor through a TIP122. The Uno pin only supplies a few mA of base current; the 1N4007 absorbs the spike when the motor is switched off.

name: L293D Forward/Stop
desc: Runs the DC motor forward for 3 s and stops for 2 s using one channel of the L293D.

name: Relay Click Test
desc: The button toggles the relay (listen for the click, watch the board LED). The red LED on the relay contacts shows the switched circuit.

name: Stepper One Revolution
desc: The 28BYJ-48 turns exactly one revolution (2048 steps), pauses, then turns back.

name: BO Motor Spin
desc: The L298N channel A spins the BO gear motor forward, stops, then spins it backwards.

name: MOSFET LED Switch
desc: The IRFZ44N switches an LED branch from a digital pin: the gate takes almost no current, the load runs through the drain.

name: Motor Speed with PWM
desc: analogWrite() ramps the motor speed up and down through the TIP122.

name: Button-Controlled Servo
desc: Each button press steps the servo by 30 degrees; after 180 it returns to 0.

name: Flyback Diode Demonstration
desc: The relay switches the motor supply on and off every 2 s. The 1N4007 across the motor gives the coil current a path when the contacts open; unplug its jumper to see why it matters on real hardware (the simulator does not model the voltage spike).

name: L293D Direction Control
desc: Each button press moves to the next state: FORWARD, BRAKE, REVERSE, COAST.

name: L298N Dual Motor Drive
desc: Channel A (DC motor) ramps up while channel B (BO motor) ramps down, then they swap directions - speed and direction are independent.

name: Warm-Hand Fan Speed Demo
desc: Warm the LM35 with your hand (raise the temperature slider): the fan speeds up in five PWM steps, one per two degrees above 27 C.

name: Temperature Fan Controller
desc: The LM35 temperature picks the motor speed: below 28 C off, 28-31 C slow, 31-34 C medium, above 34 C full speed.

name: Servo Gate
desc: A press opens the gate (90 degrees, green); it closes by itself 4 s later (red).

name: Stepper Angle Positioning
desc: Type an angle such as A90 or A-45 in the Serial Monitor (H sets home): the stepper moves to that absolute angle by the shortest number of steps.

name: Stepper Speed Ramp
desc: The stepper accelerates from 2 to 14 rpm and back down in small chunks of steps. A button press reverses the direction.

name: Relay Lamp Timer
desc: A press switches the relay (and the green lamp on its contacts) on for 6 s. Pressing again while it is on restarts the countdown.

name: Soft-Start Motor with MOSFET
desc: The IRFZ44N ramps the motor up over 3 s, runs it, then ramps down. The 10k+10k divider reports the pack voltage; the 100 uF capacitor and the flyback diode protect the supply.

name: Servo + DC Motor Combo Door
desc: A press unlocks the servo latch, the L293D motor opens the model door for 1.5 s, it waits, closes it again and the servo locks.

name: Differential Drive Demo
desc: Two motors act as the left and right wheels. Each press runs the next manoeuvre for 2.5 s: STRAIGHT, LEFT, RIGHT, SPIN, then stop.

name: Stepper Dial Pointer
desc: The stepper turns a dial pointer to show the LM35 temperature: 20 C = 0 degrees, 40 C = 270 degrees.

name: PWM Brake and Coast Comparison
desc: The motor runs for 2 s, then stops either by COASTING (enable low, outputs off) or by BRAKING (enable high, both outputs low, the motor shorts itself). A press chooses the mode. A real motor coasts for a while but stops almost at once when braked.

name: Relay Toggle with Debounce
desc: One button latches the relay on and off. Contact bounce is filtered; green = relay on, red = relay off.

name: Motor Direction Safety Interlock
desc: The button asks for the opposite direction, but the motor must first stop and stay stopped for 1.5 s (red LED blinks) - no instant reversal.

name: Capacitor Smoothing Experiment
desc: Starts and stops the motor five times and prints the lowest pack voltage seen in each start-up. Delete the purple capacitor jumpers and run again to compare how much the supply dips without the 100 uF capacitor.

name: MOSFET vs TIP122 Comparison
desc: The same motor is switched fully on by the TIP122 and then by the IRFZ44N. The divider measures the voltage left across the switch: the smaller it is, the more of the 6 V reaches the motor.

name: Stepper Half-Step vs Full-Step
desc: Press the button: the stepper turns a quarter revolution in FULL-step mode (512 steps) and again in HALF-step mode (1024 steps at the same coil rate) and prints how long each took. Half-stepping is smoother and twice as fine.

name: BO Motor Wheel Test Rig
desc: Each press runs the BO wheel forward 2 s, pauses, runs it in reverse 2 s and stops - at the next PWM level (80, 120, 160, 200, 255). Note how the speed rises with the duty cycle.

name: Automatic Fan with Hysteresis
desc: The relay switches the fan on above 30 C and off below 27 C. The 3 degree dead band stops the relay chattering around a single threshold. Green = temperature OK, red = fan running.

name: Automatic Door Controller
desc: State machine: the button starts a cycle - stepper bolt retracts, servo door opens, holds 3 s (a press extends the hold), closes, bolt locks. If the door has been open for 15 s in total, a safety timeout forces it shut and latches a fault (red blinks; press to clear).

name: Closed-Loop Temperature Fan
desc: A PI controller turns the LM35 error (temperature minus the 30 C setpoint) into PWM for the IRFZ44N-driven fan: proportional term for quick reaction, integral term to remove the remaining error. Anti-windup keeps the integral sane.

name: Two-Motor Robot Drive Brain
desc: Type F, B, L, R, X (spin) or S (stop) in the Serial Monitor - optionally followed by a speed 1-9, e.g. F7. Wheel speeds ramp smoothly towards their targets. The button is an emergency stop (red, latched; press again to release). Green blinks while moving.

name: Stepper Pick-and-Place Model
desc: A press runs the whole cycle: stepper swings the arm to the pick point, the servo gripper closes, the relay switches the "electromagnet" lamp on, the arm swings to the place point, the gripper opens, the magnet goes off and the arm returns home.

name: Elevator Simulation
desc: The stepper is the car (floors 1-3), the servo is the door. Tap the button 1-3 times to call that floor. Interlocks: the car only moves with the door closed and the door only opens when the car has stopped. Red = moving, green = door open.

name: Heat-Seeking Servo Pointer
desc: Press the button: the servo scans 0-180 degrees, averages the LM35 at each angle, then parks at the warmest direction (green). Move the temperature slider during the scan to place a "heat source".

name: Motor Soft-Start with Current-Safe Sequencing
desc: A press soft-starts the BO motor (L298N), waits until the pack voltage has recovered from the start-up dip, and only then soft-starts the DC motor (L293D) - so the two inrush currents never overlap. The next press stops both.

name: Servo Trajectory Planner
desc: The servo moves between stored waypoints (20, 150, 60, 120, 90 degrees) along an S-curve, accelerating and decelerating smoothly. The button starts or pauses the sequence; green = moving, red = idle.

name: Relay-Based Alternating Pump Logic Demo
desc: Pump A is the motor on the TIP122, pump B is the yellow lamp on the relay. Every button press is a water demand: the pump with the LOWER total run time takes it (3 s), so both wear equally. Green = A running, red = B running.

name: Stepper Position Memory
desc: A tap moves the stepper 256 steps; holding the button for 1 s sets "home" (position 0, green LED). The position is stored in EEPROM after every move and restored at the next start-up, so power cuts do not lose it.

name: Motor Stall Detection by Timing
desc: The kit has no speed sensor, so the button stands in for a rotation switch: press it to start the motor, then keep tapping it once per "revolution". If no tap arrives within 1.5 s (2.5 s at start-up) the motor is judged stalled and power is cut through the TIP122 and the relay (red). A press clears the fault.

name: PWM Frequency Explorer
desc: The motor gets 50 % duty at four different PWM frequencies: the hardware 490 Hz, then software PWM at 100, 10 and 2 Hz. Press the button to change. At 2 Hz the motor visibly pulses; at high frequency its inertia smooths the pulses into a steady speed.

name: Conveyor Belt Controller
desc: A tap starts / stops the BO-motor belt (green running, red stopped); holding the button jogs the belt slowly. While running an "item" arrives every 2.5 s and is counted; every third item the servo diverter swings across for a second.

name: Thermostat Heater/Fan Simulator
desc: Setpoint 25 C with a +/-1 C dead band. The relay (red lamp) is the heater, the motor on the TIP122 is the fan, speed rising with the excess temperature. The button cycles the mode AUTO / HEAT only / COOL only / OFF. Green = in band and idle, red = something is running.

name: Window Blind Controller
desc: The stepper winds the blind between 0 % (open) and 100 % (closed), 4096 steps in all. A tap goes to the next preset (0, 25, 50, 75, 100 %, then back to 0); holding the button is the manual override and runs the blind continuously, reversing direction on every hold. Red = moving, green = at a preset.

name: Gearbox Speed Profile Tester
desc: Each press runs both motors (DC on channel A, BO gear motor on B) through the next 4 s speed profile: LINEAR ramp, S-CURVE, STEPS or TRAPEZOID. The PWM values are printed so you can compare how gently each profile loads the gearbox.

name: Motor Control Command Language
desc: A serial interpreter for every actuator: S90 (servo angle), M1 128 (DC motor speed -255..255), M2 -100 (BO motor), T512 (stepper steps), R1 on / R1 off (relay lamp), STATUS, STOP, HELP.

name: Safety-Interlocked Machine Cycle
desc: With one button the "two-hand" start becomes a two-step start: HOLD for 1 s (arms for 2 s), then TAP. The servo guard closes before the relay (the machine lamp) switches on for 4 s. Any press during the cycle is an e-stop: relay off at once, guard stays shut, red latched; a 2 s hold resets.

name: Efficient Motor Driver Benchmark
desc: Four drivers share one motor, each used as a low-side switch. One after the other they switch it fully on while the divider measures the voltage lost across the switch: the lower the loss, the more of the 6 V reaches the motor. A ranking is printed. (The kit has no tachometer, so delivered voltage replaces measured speed.)

name: Pan-Tilt Style Sequencer
desc: The stepper is the pan base, the servo the tilt arm. HOLD the button to jog the selected axis (it reverses each time). Taps within 0.6 s: 1 = save a waypoint, 2 = switch axis (base / arm), 3 = replay the recorded sequence, any press stops the replay. Red = recording, green = replaying.

name: Gas Leak Detector
desc: The MQ-2 analog level above 40 % sounds the buzzer. Raise "Gas concentration" in the inspector.

name: Flame Detector
desc: When the flame sensor sees a flame its output goes LOW: the red LED lights and the buzzer sounds.

name: Air Quality Reader
desc: Prints the MQ-135 reading with a CLEAN / MODERATE / POOR / HAZARDOUS classification.

name: DHT22 Temperature and Humidity
desc: High-accuracy readings (0.1 degree / 0.1 %) printed every 2 s.

name: DS18B20 Probe Temperature
desc: Reads the liquid temperature from the waterproof 1-Wire probe (with its 10k pull-up).

name: Barometric Pressure Reader
desc: Prints pressure in hPa and the altitude calculated from it.

name: Rain Alarm
desc: The buzzer sounds while the rain board is more than 30 % wet.

name: Soil Moisture Reader
desc: Prints the soil moisture percentage and a DRY / MOIST / WET class.

name: Relay Switch
desc: The button toggles the relay; the red LED on the relay contacts shows the switched circuit.

name: LCD Status Message
desc: A button press toggles the LCD between 'SAFE' and 'DANGER'.

name: LPG Alarm with LCD
desc: The gas level is shown on the LCD. At 50 % the alarm starts (buzzer + red LED) and the relay cuts the gas supply; it only clears again below 30 % (hysteresis).

name: Smoke and Flame Fire Alarm
desc: Flame alone (or smoke alone) is a WARNING (red blinks, slow beeps). Smoke AND flame together is a FIRE ALARM (red steady, continuous buzzer). Green = all clear.

name: Air Quality Index Display
desc: The MQ-135 level is mapped to a 0-500 AQI-like number with a category on the LCD. Green up to AQI 100, red above.

name: Weather Station Basic
desc: Three LCD pages, changed with the button: temperature and humidity (DHT22), pressure and altitude (BMP280), and the two temperature readings side by side.

name: Waterproof Thermometer with Alarm
desc: The probe temperature is shown on the LCD. Outside the 18-30 C window the red LED and buzzer alarm (TOO COLD / TOO HOT).

name: Water Pump on Dry Soil
desc: The pump (TIP122 + flyback diode) starts when the soil falls below 30 % and stops above 50 %. The green LED shows the pump is running.

name: Rain-Triggered Relay
desc: The relay closes (a "cover" motor) only after rain has been detected for 3 s, and opens again after 3 s without rain. Red = cover closed, green = open.

name: Pressure Trend Weather Predictor
desc: Every 15 s (a demo for 3 hours) the pressure is compared with the previous sample: falling more than 1 hPa = RAIN LIKELY (red), rising = FAIR (green), otherwise STEADY. Move the pressure slider to try it.

name: Gas Level Bar Graph
desc: The MQ-2 level is drawn as a 16-character bar on the second LCD row.

name: Fire Alarm with Relay Shutoff
desc: A flame latches the alarm: the relay cuts the power, the siren sounds and the red LED lights. The alarm stays on after the flame is gone until the button is pressed with no flame present.

name: Indoor Climate Monitor
desc: Comfort rating from the DHT22: 20-26 C and 30-60 % humidity is COMFORTABLE (green); otherwise the LCD names the problem (too hot / cold / humid / dry) and the red LED lights.

name: Pump Dry-Run Protection
desc: The pump runs when the soil is dry. If after 8 s of running the soil has not become at least 5 % wetter (empty tank, blocked pipe) the pump is stopped, the red LED locks out and it retries after a 20 s cool-down.

name: MQ Sensor Warm-Up and Baseline
desc: The MQ heaters need a warm-up (8 s here, many minutes in real life - green blinks). Then press the button in clean air: 30 readings of each sensor are averaged and stored in EEPROM as the baseline, and the sketch reports the change from baseline.

name: Temperature Compare DS18B20 vs DHT22
desc: Both sensors are logged every 2 s with their difference and the running average offset (the DS18B20 is the reference).

name: Rain Intensity Meter
desc: Wetness is quantified as NONE / LIGHT / MODERATE / HEAVY with the percentage and a bar on the LCD.

name: Alarm Escalation with Buzzer Patterns
desc: Gas levels map to different alarms: 25-50 % LOW (one short beep every 1.5 s), 50-75 % MEDIUM (two beeps a second), over 75 % HIGH (continuous). Green = safe.

name: Soil Moisture Display
desc: The moisture percentage and a short bar are shown on the LCD; the green "water" LED lights when the soil drops below 35 %.

name: Altitude Meter
desc: Relative altitude from the BMP280 pressure (average of 8 readings). Press the button to zero it at the current height; change the pressure slider to climb (about -0.12 hPa per metre).

name: Relay Exhaust Fan Trigger (Indicator)
desc: The relay (the exhaust fan) switches on when the MQ-135 air quality level exceeds 55 % and off again below 40 %. Red = fan running, green = air good.

name: Humidity Threshold Alarm
desc: The humidity must stay between 30 % and 70 % (fixed limits, no pot). Outside the range the LCD says TOO DRY / TOO HUMID, the red LED lights and the buzzer chirps.

name: Complete Home Safety Panel
desc: Four zones: gas, fire, high temperature (over 45 C) and rain (information only). Gas and fire alarms are LATCHED and cut the supply with the relay. The button silences the buzzer; once the cause has cleared a second press resets the latches. Green = all clear.

name: Environmental Monitoring Station
desc: Logs air quality, air temperature, humidity, pressure and probe temperature every 2 s. The button changes the LCD page; the pressure trend arrow (over the last 6 samples) and alarm thresholds (AQI over 150, temperature over 35 C, humidity over 85 %) are marked with "!".

name: Automated Irrigation Controller
desc: Waters when the soil is below 30 %, but not if it is raining (over 20 % wet), too hot (over 35 C, evaporation) or within 15 s of the last run. Stops at 55 %. Flood protection (soil over 85 %) and dry-run protection (no 3 % rise within 6 s) lock the pump (red).

name: Smart Greenhouse Rules Engine
desc: A rule table (sensor, comparison, threshold, action) is evaluated every pass: soil < 35 -> pump; air > 30 C or humidity > 85 % -> fan (relay); root-zone probe < 12 C or > 32 C, or soil > 85 % -> alerts. A waterlogged-soil rule inhibits the pump. The LCD lists the active rules.

name: Fire Detection with Sensor Fusion
desc: A score combines smoke (up to 50), flame (+40) and the temperature rise over the last 10 s (up to +30). 30+ is WATCH; 60+ for 3 samples in a row (1 per second) is a FIRE ALARM (relay, siren, red, latched). A single spike never alarms. The button resets.

name: Gas Safety with Auto Valve Relay and Self-Test
desc: The relay holds the gas valve OPEN (fail-safe: no power = shut). Gas over 60 % closes it, with siren and red; a tap re-opens it once the gas is below 30 %. HOLD the button for 1.5 s for a self-test (beep, relay click, sensor plausibility). The last four events are logged with timestamps.

name: Weather Forecaster
desc: The pressure change over a 12 s window (standing in for 3 hours), the humidity and the rain sensor combine into a forecast text: STORM LIKELY, RAIN IN 12 h, RAIN NOW / CLEARING, FAIR, CLOUDY or STABLE. The button switches between the forecast and the raw data.

name: Indoor Air Ventilation Controller
desc: In AUTO the fan relay switches on when the AQI exceeds 60 or humidity exceeds 75 %, and off only when AQI < 40 and humidity < 65 % (hysteresis). The button cycles AUTO / ON / OFF manual overrides. Red = fan running, green = fan off.

name: Aquarium Monitor
desc: The probe watches the water temperature (24-28 C) and the rain-board strip is the water-level gauge. Below 30 % level the top-up pump runs until 60 %. The buzzer sounds for a temperature alarm or a pump timeout (10 s without the level recovering = reservoir empty).

name: Sensor Calibration Suite
desc: A guided two-point calibration: the LCD asks for soil dry / in water, rain board dry / wet, then MQ-2 and MQ-135 in clean air; each button press records the reading (average of 10). The six values are stored in EEPROM, after which calibrated percentages are shown live. HOLD the button 2 s to recalibrate.

name: Pollution Event Logger
desc: An EVENT starts when either gas sensor passes 40 % and ends below 30 %. For each event the peak level, which sensor caused it and the duration are logged (last 5 kept) with running statistics. A chirp marks every new event. The button pages: live / last event / statistics.

name: Storm Alert System
desc: Three storm factors: pressure fell by 1.5 hPa or more in the last 15 s window (standing in for 3 h), the rain board is over 30 % wet, humidity is over 75 %. Two factors = WATCH (red blinks), all three = STORM WARNING (red steady + siren). Green = calm.

name: Safe Room Monitor
desc: An occupancy-agnostic air check: the ventilation relay switches on when the AQI exceeds 55 or the temperature exceeds 30 C (off again below AQI 40 and 28 C). The buzzer alarms for flammable gas over 50 % or a room temperature over 35 C.

name: Fault-Tolerant Sensor Hub
desc: Three sensors measure the temperature. Each is checked for validity and plausibility (a reading more than 4 C from the median of the three is SUSPECT, an impossible value or NaN is FAILED); the hub then averages only the healthy ones and keeps working, naming the bad sensor. The MQ-2 is checked for a stuck-at-rail reading. Green = all healthy, red = degraded.

name: Rain Water Harvest Controller
desc: The rain board decides when to collect: the inlet relay opens while it is raining and the tank (the soil probe as level gauge) is below 90 %. The pump transfers water to storage when the tank is above 60 % until it is below 25 %. If the pump runs 8 s without the tank falling by 3 %, the dry-run lock stops it (red). Tank over 90 % shows overflow (red).

name: Emergency Warning Beacon
desc: Priority-based patterns: FIRE (flame) = fast red flashing + siren + relay beacon on; GAS (over 50 %) = slow red + double beeps + relay beacon flashing; CAUTION (30-50 % gas) = green blinks. The button acknowledges (silences the buzzer; lights stay) - a higher priority event un-acknowledges it.

name: Dew and Frost Risk Estimator
desc: The DHT22 gives air temperature and humidity, from which the dew point is computed (Magnus formula). The DS18B20 is the surface temperature. Surface within 2 C of the dew point = DEW RISK; the same at or below 0 C = FROST RISK. Green = safe, red = risk.

name: Predictive Maintenance Demo
desc: Each button press waters for 5 s and measures how much the soil moisture rose. The first run sets the baseline; later runs are compared with it. Total run time is tracked, and when the response falls below 50 % of the baseline the red LED and the LCD predict a clogged line.

name: Multi-Page Safety Dashboard
desc: Four LCD pages (gases, flame and status, climate, pressure) selected with the button. Whenever a danger exists (gas over 50 %, flame, AQI over 150, humidity over 90 %) an alert banner replaces the first row on every page.

name: Safety Compliance Self-Check
desc: At boot every device is tested in turn and the result is shown on the LCD and printed: gas sensors (heated, in range), flame (idle), rain (dry), soil (in range), DHT22, DS18B20, BMP280 (plausible values), then a relay click and a buzzer beep. A PASS / FAIL summary lists the failures.

name: Bluetooth LED Control
desc: Send 1 / ON or 0 / OFF from the phone terminal (HC-05 inspector) to switch the red LED. The 10k + 20k divider brings the Uno 5 V TX down to the 3.3 V the module accepts.

name: Bluetooth Echo
desc: Text typed on the phone is printed on the Serial Monitor and echoed back to the phone.

name: IR Remote Key Reader
desc: Prints the code of every remote button you press in the IR remote inspector.

name: IR LED Toggle
desc: The "1" key of the remote toggles the green LED.

name: NodeMCU Blink
desc: Blinks the on-board blue LED of the ESP8266 NodeMCU (it is active LOW).

name: NodeMCU Wi-Fi Scan
desc: Scans for Wi-Fi networks and prints name, signal strength and security. The networks "in range" are a property of the NodeMCU (select it in the inspector).

name: Level Converter Test
desc: The Uno drives a 5 V signal that passes through the level converter to a NodeMCU input (3.3 V logic). The NodeMCU reports what it sees; the Uno reports what it sends.

name: NRF24 Module Check
desc: Both nRF24L01 radios run from the 3.3 V AMS1117 (a 5 V supply would destroy them). The sketch initialises each, prints the status registers and sends a ping from radio A that radio B receives.

name: Relay via Bluetooth
desc: Phone commands RELAY ON / RELAY OFF (or 1 / 0) switch the relay; the red LED mirrors it.

name: Servo via Bluetooth
desc: Send a number 0-180 from the phone and the servo turns to that angle.

name: Bluetooth LED Dimmer
desc: The phone sends a brightness 0-100 (like a slider value) and the red LED follows it with PWM.

name: Bluetooth Sensor Data to Phone
desc: The DHT11 temperature and humidity are sent to the phone every 3 s; typing READ asks for an immediate reading.

name: IR Remote Controlled Servo
desc: PREV / NEXT keys turn the servo 15 degrees left / right and PLAY centres it.

name: IR Remote Relay Switch
desc: The CH key (the remote's power button) toggles the relay; the green LED shows its state.

name: NRF24 Transmitter
desc: Radio A transmits the DHT11 reading every 2 s as a text packet; radio B (a second node on the same Uno) receives it and prints it. Raise "Packet loss" on a radio to see failed transmissions.

name: NRF24 Receiver on NodeMCU
desc: The Uno sends a numbered packet every 2 s; the NodeMCU receives and prints it. Two sketches, two boards - select each board to read its code.

name: Wi-Fi Web LED Control
desc: The NodeMCU joins the Wi-Fi network and hosts a page with ON / OFF links for an LED. Use the "Browser" box in the NodeMCU inspector (GET /, /on, /off).

name: Wi-Fi Temperature Web Page
desc: The NodeMCU serves the DHT11 temperature and humidity on a local web page (the DHT11 data line goes through the level converter because the sensor runs at 5 V).

name: Bluetooth Command Parser
desc: Commands 'LED1' / 'LED0', 'SERVO 90' and 'RELAY ON' / 'RELAY OFF' are parsed and executed; unknown commands get an error reply.

name: Remote Door Lock
desc: The phone commands LOCK / UNLOCK move the servo bolt (0 = locked, 90 = unlocked); the LCD and the red / green LEDs show the state.

name: LCD Message Receiver
desc: Text typed on the phone appears on the LCD (long messages are split over the two rows).

name: Level-Shifted UNO to NodeMCU Serial
desc: The Uno (5 V) and the NodeMCU (3.3 V) exchange text through the level converter: the Uno sends PING n every second and the NodeMCU answers ACK n.

name: NRF24 Two-Way Chat
desc: Type a message in the Serial Monitor of either board and it appears in the other board's monitor over the radio link.

name: IR Remote Number Entry
desc: Digits typed on the remote are shown on the LCD (up to 8). CH clears, PLAY accepts the number and shows its double.

name: Wireless Button Doorbell
desc: The button on the Uno (node A) sends RING over the nRF24 link; the NodeMCU (node B) flashes its red LED for 3 s.

name: Phone Alarm Notification
desc: When the temperature goes above 30 C (or humidity above 80 %) the red LED lights and an ALERT text is sent to the phone once; an all-clear follows when it passes.

name: Wi-Fi Relay Control
desc: A NodeMCU web page switches a 5 V relay; the 3.3 V GPIO drives the relay input through the level converter.

name: Bluetooth Servo Joystick
desc: The phone sends "x,y" pairs (0-180 each, like an on-screen joystick); the servo glides to x in small steps, y is reported back.

name: NodeMCU Wi-Fi Status LCD
desc: The LCD shows the connection state, then the IP address and signal strength once connected.

name: Remote Temperature Display
desc: The Uno reads the DHT11 and sends the temperature over the nRF24 radio; the NodeMCU shows it on its LCD (and flags "no signal" if packets stop).

name: Bluetooth Home Automation Panel
desc: One phone-controlled panel: RELAY ON/OFF, SERVO <angle>, RED ON/OFF, GREEN ON/OFF and STATUS (the module replies with everything). The LCD mirrors the state.

name: IoT Weather Node over Wi-Fi
desc: The NodeMCU serves a dashboard page at / and a JSON endpoint at /json with the DHT11 data (the sensor runs at 5 V; its data line passes the level converter).

name: NRF24 Sensor Network Gateway
desc: The Uno sensor node radios its DHT11 reading to the NodeMCU gateway, which serves the latest value over Wi-Fi (/ and /json) and echoes each packet back to the Uno through the level converter serial link.

name: Secure Remote Door Lock
desc: Two factors open the lock: the PIN (send PIN 1234 from the phone) and a fresh rolling code from the NodeMCU key fob. Every fob code is used once - a replayed (old) code is rejected. The fob sends the next code every 8 s; type R in the fob's monitor to replay the last one.

name: IR + Bluetooth Dual Remote Appliance Control
desc: Both the IR remote (CH toggles) and the phone (ON / OFF) control the relay. Priority rule: after any IR command the local remote wins for 10 s and phone commands are refused. The LCD shows the state and who has priority.

name: Wi-Fi Controlled Servo Radar Display Page
desc: A web page sets the servo angle (/angle?deg=NN) and a status endpoint reports the current angle and how many requests were handled. The servo signal passes through the level converter.

name: Wireless Alarm System
desc: A contact sensor (the button on the NodeMCU: pressed = door open) radios OPEN / CLOSED to the Uno. While armed an OPEN triggers the siren (red flashes fast) and an ALERT text to the phone; the phone can ARM / DISARM. Green = armed and secure.

name: OTA-Style Settings Manager
desc: Settings (BRI brightness, INT interval, THR threshold) are edited over Bluetooth with a checksum: send "SET BRI 120*CS" where CS is the 2-digit hex XOR of the text before the star; bad checksums are refused. GET lists the settings; values are stored in EEPROM.

name: Master-Slave Command Bus
desc: The Uno master sends framed commands "#seq,cmd,arg,checksum" over the radio and waits for an ACK frame from the NodeMCU slave, retrying up to 3 times. The slave verifies the checksum, executes (toggles its on-board LED) and acknowledges. Raise "Packet loss" on a radio to see retries.

name: Wi-Fi Time Display Clock
desc: The NodeMCU joins Wi-Fi, gets the time with NTP (IST, UTC+5:30, taken from the PC clock in the simulator) and sends "TIME hh:mm:ss" to the Uno every second through the level converter; the Uno shows it on the LCD.

name: Phone Data Logger
desc: Every 5 s a protocol line "LOG,<seconds>,<temp>,<hum>" is sent to the phone. The button inserts an "EVENT" marker line. The last 10 samples are kept: DUMP replays them, CLEAR empties the log.

name: Wireless Light Show Controller
desc: Four animations - 1 alternate flash, 2 chase with servo sweep, 3 breathing red, 4 all off - selected by the phone ("SHOW 2") or by the number keys of the IR remote.

name: NRF24 Range and Packet-Loss Tester
desc: The Uno sends 50 numbered packets (one every 150 ms) and counts the acknowledgements; the LCD shows sent / acknowledged and the loss percentage per run. The NodeMCU counts what it received and spots sequence gaps. Raise "Packet loss" on a radio to model distance.

name: Multi-Protocol Gateway
desc: IR keys 1-3, phone commands "ACT n" and radio packets "ACT n" (typed in the NodeMCU monitor) all go into one action queue; the main loop executes the queue in arrival order and logs the source of each action.

name: Remote Greenhouse Controller (Demo Loads)
desc: A Wi-Fi dashboard (/) shows the DHT11 climate and switches the relay load: /fan/on, /fan/off or /auto (fan on above 28 C). /json returns the data. The LCD shows climate and the relay mode. Sensor and relay both go through the level converter.

name: Encrypted Message Link
desc: The button on the Uno cycles through three messages; each is XOR-encrypted with a shared key (0x5A), sent as hex over the radio, and shown on the LCD (plain / cipher). The NodeMCU prints the intercepted cipher text and the decrypted message.

name: Smart Remote Hub with Learning
desc: IR learning: press the button to pick an action (relay toggle / servo 0 / servo 180) and press a remote key to bind it. Bluetooth macros: REC, then action words (RELAY, SERVO0, SERVO180), then END; PLAY runs them one second apart.

name: Wireless Fault Reporter
desc: The NodeMCU sends a heartbeat every 2 s. The Uno raises a FAULT (red blinks, phone notice) when 7 s pass without one and reports recovery. In the NodeMCU monitor type x to simulate a node failure (and x again to bring it back).

name: Wi-Fi Access Point Configuration Portal
desc: The NodeMCU starts its own access point "JR_Setup" and serves a form; /set?name=...&val=... forwards "SET name val" to the Uno over the level-shifted serial link, where it is shown on the LCD and stored in EEPROM.

name: Wireless System Self-Test Suite
desc: Tests run in turn and are reported on the LCD and Serial Monitor: HC-05 (AT -> OK), nRF24 radio round trip to the NodeMCU, the level-shifted NodeMCU link, the IR receiver (press any remote key within 8 s), the relay click and the LCD. Ends with a PASS / FAIL summary.

name: RFID Card UID Reader
desc: Select the RC522 and tick "Card on reader": the UID of the card (editable in the inspector) is printed on the Serial Monitor.

name: RFID Access LED
desc: The green LED lights for the authorised UID (DE AD BE EF), the red LED for any other card.

name: RTC Time Display
desc: Prints the date and time from the DS3231 every second (the simulated RTC follows the PC clock).

name: LCD Clock
desc: The date on the first LCD row and the running time on the second.

name: Servo Lock Test
desc: Each press of the button moves the servo between the locked (0 deg) and unlocked (90 deg) positions.

name: Weight Reader
desc: Tares the empty platform at start-up, then prints the weight in grams (move the "Weight on cell" slider in the HX711 inspector).

name: Voltage and Current Reader
desc: Switches the blue LED load on and prints the INA219 bus voltage, current and power. The load current flows through the INA219 shunt.

name: MPU6050 Tilt Reader
desc: Prints the acceleration (g), the rotation rate and the tilt angle. Drag the AX / AY / AZ sliders in the MPU6050 inspector.

name: Heart-Rate Raw Signal
desc: Streams the raw IR and red photodiode counts. With a finger on the sensor the IR value pulses with each heartbeat.

name: OLED Hello
desc: Shows a greeting in two text sizes and draws a frame on the 128x64 OLED.

name: RFID Door Lock
desc: The authorised card (DE AD BE EF) opens the servo latch and the relay strike for 3 s with one beep; any other card gets three beeps.

name: RFID Attendance with Time-Stamp
desc: Every card swipe is logged on the Serial Monitor with the RTC date and time, and the last swipe is shown on the LCD.

name: Access Log on LCD
desc: Shows the last card, whether it was GRANTED or DENIED and the time of the swipe on the LCD.

name: Digital Weighing Scale
desc: The weight in grams on the LCD. Press the button to tare (zero) the scale with the pan empty or with a container on it.

name: Overload Alarm Scale
desc: Weighs on the LCD; above the 500 g limit the red LED lights and the buzzer sounds until the load is removed.

name: Power Meter
desc: The OLED shows the INA219 voltage, current and power, plus the energy used so far (mWh) integrated over time.

name: Tilt Alarm
desc: When the board is tilted more than 30 degrees (raise AX or lower AZ in the MPU6050 inspector) the red LED lights and the buzzer sounds.

name: Step/Motion Counter
desc: Counts a step every time the total acceleration jumps above 1.3 g (a peak). Raise AZ to 1.6 g and back to simulate a step.

name: Pulse Rate Display
desc: Detects heartbeats in the MAX30102 IR signal and shows the averaged BPM on the OLED (set a different "Heart rate" in the inspector).

name: Alarm Clock
desc: The alarm is armed for 20 s after power-up so you can see it ring. Press the button to snooze it for 15 s.

name: Timed Relay Schedule
desc: The relay is ON from second 10 to second 40 of every minute (a fast demo schedule - swap second() for hour() / minute() for a daily timetable). The LCD shows the clock and the relay state.

name: RFID Add/Remove Master Card
desc: The master card (AA BB CC DD) cycles NORMAL -> ADD -> REMOVE. In ADD mode the next card is stored in EEPROM, in REMOVE mode it is deleted. Stored cards open the door (green), others do not (red).

name: Smart Locker with Weight Check
desc: An authorised card opens and closes the locker door (servo). The LCD always reports the weight of the contents measured by the load cell.

name: Battery Voltage Monitor
desc: The INA219 measures the supply voltage while a small load runs. Above LOW_V the green LED is on; below it the red LED and buzzer warn (raise LOW_V to 5.0 in the code to see the warning).

name: IMU Level Bubble on OLED
desc: A digital spirit level: the bubble moves on the OLED as you change AX / AY in the MPU6050 inspector and sits in the centre ring when the board is level.

name: Access Denied Lockout
desc: Three wrong cards in a row start a 30 s lockout: the buzzer pulses, the red LED lights and every card is ignored while the LCD counts down.

name: Fall Detector Demo
desc: A fall is free-fall (total acceleration below 0.4 g) followed by an impact (above 2 g) within half a second. Try AZ = 0.1 then AZ = 2.5 in the inspector.

name: SpO2 Estimate Display
desc: Averages red and IR light over about a second and turns their ratio into an approximate SpO2 (teaching calibration), next to the BPM. Change "SpO2" and "Heart rate" in the inspector.

name: Data Logger with Timestamp
desc: Logs one CSV line every 2 s: the RTC date and time, the INA219 voltage and the load current. Copy the Serial Monitor text into a spreadsheet.

name: Kitchen Scale with Unit Switching
desc: A short press switches between grams and ounces, a long press (hold 1 s) tares the scale.

name: Complete Smart Locker
desc: RFID opens the locker (servo latch + relay strike), the load cell reports what was put in or taken out, every event is logged with the RTC time and the OLED shows the status.

name: Attendance System with Reports
desc: Three registered cards swipe IN and OUT. Visits and time present are kept per user in EEPROM (reset each new day); press the button to print the daily report on the Serial Monitor.

name: Time-Based Access Control
desc: Staff may enter during seconds 0-39 of every minute, the visitor card during seconds 20-49 (a fast demo: change second() to hour() for real opening hours). Outside its window a card is refused.

name: Energy Monitor and Logger
desc: Integrates the INA219 power into energy (mWh), shows it on the OLED and logs a time-stamped line every 10 s (use 3600 for an hourly log). The button resets the energy counter.

name: Motion-Aware Power Saver
desc: While the board moves the OLED and the load stay on. After 5 s without motion both switch off, and the INA219 proves the saving (current falls to about 0). Shake the board with the AX slider to wake it.

name: Posture and Tilt Coach
desc: Tilting past 20 degrees for 3 s counts as a slouch: red LED and beeps. When you sit up again the slouch is logged with its start time and duration.

name: Health Monitor
desc: BPM and SpO2 from the MAX30102 with motion rejection: while the MPU6050 sees movement the readings are discarded. The OLED draws a BPM trend and the buzzer warns about low SpO2 or an abnormal pulse.

name: Smart Medication Box
desc: A dose falls due 25 s after start-up. The box beeps and stays locked until the carer card opens the lid; the load cell then checks that 3-20 g of pills were taken before the card closes it again.

name: Industrial Weighing Station
desc: Short press = next mode: WEIGH (long press tares), COUNT (long press adds the item to the batch), CAL (long press calibrates against a 200 g mass) and REPORT (long press prints and clears the batch). Above 800 g the relay trips and latches.

name: Vibration Monitor
desc: Measures the RMS of the acceleration ripple over 40 samples and shows it in milli-g. Above 200 mg the buzzer sounds and the event is logged with the RTC time.

name: Secure Vault Alarm
desc: The owner card arms and disarms the vault. While armed, shaking the MPU6050, changing the weight on the load cell or presenting a wrong card latches the alarm (relay + buzzer) until the owner card is swiped.

name: Calibration Manager
desc: A short press selects TARE / SPAN 200 g / CURRENT ZERO / IMU ZERO, a long press performs and saves it in EEPROM. The stored values are loaded again at every start-up.

name: Appliance Usage Tracker
desc: The relay switches the appliance (the blue LED load measured by the INA219). Each use is logged with RTC times, duration and energy; after 20 s the relay cuts the power. The button switches it on again.

name: Wearable Prototype Dashboard
desc: A four-page OLED dashboard (time, heart rate, steps, battery) paged with the button. The pulse sensor and step counter keep running in the background whichever page is shown.

name: Fall Detection and Alert
desc: A hard impact followed by a lying-down orientation starts an 8 s pre-alarm (beeps). Press the button to cancel; otherwise the alarm escalates: relay (external siren / dialer), continuous buzzer and red LED.

name: Smart Door with Two-Factor Auth
desc: Factor 1: the owner card. Factor 2: a 3-press PIN on the button - short, LONG, short. Both correct opens the servo and relay; every attempt is logged with the RTC time.

name: Sample-Weight Dispensing Controller
desc: Short press picks the target (25 / 50 / 100 / 200 g), long press tares and starts: the gate (servo) and feeder (relay) run until the target minus the learned in-flight amount is reached. After settling, the controller corrects its own anticipation.

name: Multi-Sensor Black Box Recorder
desc: Records acceleration, current and heart rate in a rolling buffer (20 samples, 5 per second). An impact above 0.6 g or the button freezes the buffer after 10 more samples and dumps it on the Serial Monitor with the RTC time stamp.

name: Capstone: Integrated Smart-Locker System
desc: Everything together: RFID opens the locker (servo + relay strike), the load cell checks the contents, the MPU6050 raises a tamper alarm while it is locked, the INA219 monitors the electronics, the RTC time-stamps the events, the LCD shows the status and the OLED the power, tilt and event log.

name: Weigh-and-Log Station
desc: Put an item on the pan and press the button: its weight is logged with the RTC time stamp and added to the running total on the LCD. Remove the item before the next one. A long press starts a new batch (and tares).
